name_note: GTDB also places in this species single genomes deposited at NCBI as Corynebacterium aurimucosum and Corynebacterium tuberculostearicum; published work treats C. kefirresidentii and C. tuberculostearicum as members of one species complex.

sentences.text: Corynebacterium kefirresidentii was reported as a novel Corynebacterium species from a strain, SB, isolated from kefir grains collected in Germany.
A comparative genomics study describes Corynebacterium as a dominant member of the human skin microbiome and places this species, with Corynebacterium tuberculostearicum, in a narrow species complex.
That study reported through metagenomics that individual species of the complex can associate with specific body sites.

It also reported that Corynebacterium kefirresidentii increases in relative abundance during atopic dermatitis flares, and that most genomes of the species encode a colocalized set of putative virulence genes.
